lessons.title: Paris, 2000: La Octava
lessons.subtitle: Real Madrid win the first all-Spanish European Cup final

story.title: A final between Spanish rivals
story.body: Real Madrid and Valencia met in the European Cup final in Paris on 24 May 2000.

story.title: Three goals, a clean sheet
story.body: Fernando Morientes, Steve McManaman and Raúl scored in a 3–0 victory, giving Madrid its eighth European Cup.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which Spanish club did Real Madrid defeat in the 2000 European Cup final?
facts.scope: The first all-Spanish European Cup final, played in Paris on 24 May 2000.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid records Valencia as its opponent in the 2000 final.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Real Madrid’s 2000 European Cup final win?
facts.scope: The European Cup final against Valencia.
facts.evidence: The official account gives the final score as 3–0.

facts.label: Third scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Real Madrid’s third goal in the final?
facts.scope: The 2000 final in Paris, after Morientes and McManaman scored.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid says Raúl completed the 3–0 win.

story.title: A final in Wales
story.body: Real Madrid met Juventus in Cardiff on 3 June 2017.

story.title: Ronaldo decides it
story.body: Cristiano Ronaldo scored twice in a 4–1 win and was named man of the match.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Real Madrid beat in the 2017 Champions League final?
facts.scope: The 2017 final in Cardiff.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid records a 4–1 final victory over Juventus.

facts.label: Ronaldo’s final goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Cristiano Ronaldo score in the final?
facts.scope: Ronaldo’s contribution to the 3 June 2017 final.
facts.evidence: The club says Ronaldo’s two goals earned him man of the match.

facts.label: Final award
facts.prompt: Which award did Ronaldo receive for his performance in Cardiff?
facts.scope: The individual award for the 2017 Champions League final.
facts.evidence: The official final report names Ronaldo man of the match.

story.title: Goals in every competition
story.body: Real Madrid’s profile records Ronaldo’s goals across LaLiga, the Champions League, domestic cups and international club competitions.

story.title: An extraordinary peak
story.body: The club also records 61 goals in a single season and six Champions League top-scorer awards during his Madrid years.

facts.label: Single-season record
facts.prompt: How many goals did Ronaldo score in his most prolific Real Madrid season?
facts.scope: Ronaldo’s Real Madrid single-season scoring record.
facts.evidence: The profile says 61 was the most goals by a Real Madrid player in one season.

facts.label: Champions League scoring awards
facts.prompt: How many times did Ronaldo finish as Champions League top scorer while at Madrid?
facts.scope: His Real Madrid Champions League campaigns.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid records six occasions as competition top scorer.

facts.label: Ballon d’Or awards
facts.prompt: How many Ballon d’Or awards does the Real Madrid profile list for Ronaldo?
facts.scope: Individual awards recorded during his Real Madrid career.
facts.evidence: The profile lists four Ballons d’Or.

lessons.title: Ramos scores in another world final
lessons.subtitle: Real Madrid beat Al Ain in 2018

story.title: The final in Abu Dhabi
story.body: Real Madrid faced Al Ain in the 2018 FIFA Club World Cup final.

story.title: A captain’s header
story.body: Ramos scored Madrid’s third goal as the team won 4–1 and claimed its fourth Club World Cup.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Real Madrid defeat in the 2018 Club World Cup final?
facts.scope: The final played in Abu Dhabi in December 2018.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid’s account names Al Ain as the final opponent.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score in the 2018 Club World Cup final?
facts.scope: Real Madrid’s final against Al Ain.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid’s 2024 retrospective gives the final as 4-1 and lists the goals, including Ramos’s third.

facts.label: Ramos’s goal
facts.prompt: Which goal did Ramos score in the final?
facts.scope: Ramos’s headed goal in the 2018 final.
facts.evidence: The club states Ramos scored Madrid’s third goal.

story.title: Repeated World XI selection
story.body: Ramos was selected for the FIFA FIFPro World 11 eleven times.

story.title: Defensive distinction
story.body: He was named the Champions League’s best defender in both 2017 and 2018, and earned the Club World Cup Golden Ball in 2014.

facts.label: FIFA FIFPro World 11
facts.prompt: How many times was Ramos selected for the FIFA FIFPro World 11?
facts.scope: The selections listed in his Real Madrid profile through 2020.
facts.evidence: The profile enumerates eleven World 11 selections.

facts.label: Champions League defender award
facts.prompt: In which two years was Ramos named the Champions League’s best defender?
facts.scope: His back-to-back individual defensive awards.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid lists the award years as 2017 and 2018.

facts.label: Club World Cup award
facts.prompt: Which individual award did Ramos win at the 2014 Club World Cup?
facts.scope: Ramos’s individual award at the 2014 tournament.
facts.evidence: The profile records his 2014 Club World Cup Golden Ball.

lessons.title: Casillas takes over in Glasgow
lessons.subtitle: A decisive substitute appearance in the 2002 final

story.title: An injury changes the final
story.body: Real Madrid met Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League final at Hampden Park on 15 May 2002.

story.title: Casillas enters the match
story.body: After César was injured, Casillas came on and made key saves as Madrid protected its 2–1 lead.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Real Madrid face in the 2002 Champions League final?
facts.scope: The final at Hampden Park in Glasgow.
facts.evidence: The club identifies Bayer Leverkusen as the opponent.

facts.label: Goalkeeper substitution
facts.prompt: Which goalkeeper did Casillas replace in the final?
facts.scope: The change made after the starting goalkeeper was injured.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid says César was replaced by Casillas.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score in Real Madrid’s 2002 victory?
facts.scope: The 2002 Champions League final.
facts.evidence: The club records a 2–1 win over Leverkusen.

story.title: A decorated international
story.body: Casillas won the World Cup and two European Championships with Spain.

story.title: A global goalkeeper award
story.body: He was selected for the FIFA FIFPro World XI five times and named the world’s best goalkeeper by IFFHS five times.

facts.label: European Championships
facts.prompt: How many European Championships did Casillas win with Spain?
facts.scope: Spain’s senior men’s team honours during Casillas’s international career.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid lists two European Championships.

facts.label: FIFA FIFPro World XI
facts.prompt: How many times was Casillas included in the FIFA FIFPro World XI?
facts.scope: The individual selections listed in his Real Madrid profile.
facts.evidence: The club records five selections.

facts.label: IFFHS goalkeeper award
facts.prompt: How many times did Casillas win the IFFHS world’s best goalkeeper award?
facts.scope: Individual goalkeeper awards listed in his Real Madrid profile.
facts.evidence: The profile records five IFFHS best-goalkeeper awards.

lessons.title: Raúl’s double at Old Trafford
lessons.subtitle: Redondo sets up a quarter-final classic

story.title: A difficult away tie
story.body: Madrid visited Manchester United in the Champions League quarter-final on 19 April 2000 after a goalless first leg.

story.title: Two goals settle it
story.body: Raúl scored twice in a 3–2 win at Old Trafford, helping Madrid advance toward the eighth European Cup.

facts.label: Opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Madrid beat at Old Trafford in April 2000?
facts.scope: The second leg of the 2000 Champions League quarter-final.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid records the 3–2 away win against Manchester United.

facts.label: Match score
facts.prompt: What was the score at Old Trafford?
facts.scope: The quarter-final second leg in Manchester.
facts.evidence: The official account gives the score as 3–2.

facts.label: Raúl’s goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Raúl score in the match?
facts.scope: Raúl’s contribution to Madrid’s quarter-final win.
facts.evidence: He scored in the 50th and 52nd minutes.

lessons.title: Raúl’s long Madrid era
lessons.subtitle: Sixteen seasons and six league titles

story.title: A first-team mainstay
story.body: Raúl represented Real Madrid for 16 seasons, from his promotion to the first team in 1994 until 2010.

story.title: Domestic success
story.body: Among his honours were six LaLiga titles and two Intercontinental Cups.

facts.label: Madrid seasons
facts.prompt: How many seasons did Raúl play for Real Madrid?
facts.scope: His completed Real Madrid playing spell.
facts.evidence: The club states that he played 16 seasons.

facts.label: LaLiga titles
facts.prompt: How many LaLiga titles did Raúl win with Madrid?
facts.scope: His Madrid honours during 1994–2010.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid lists six LaLiga titles.

facts.label: Intercontinental Cups
facts.prompt: How many Intercontinental Cups did Raúl win with Madrid?
facts.scope: His Madrid honours.
facts.evidence: The club lists two Intercontinental Cups.

lessons.title: Benzema helps finish the City comeback
lessons.subtitle: A penalty sends Madrid into the final

story.title: Madrid trail late
story.body: In the Champions League semi-final second leg on 4 May 2022, Madrid were behind Manchester City 1–0 in the 89th minute.

story.title: Extra time decides the tie
story.body: After Rodrygo’s two late goals forced extra time, Benzema converted a penalty to send Madrid through.

facts.label: Semi-final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Madrid overcome in the 2022 semi-final?
facts.scope: The Champions League semi-final second leg at the Bernabéu.
facts.evidence: The match report identifies Manchester City as the opponent.

facts.label: Decisive action
facts.prompt: How did Benzema help Madrid win the tie in extra time?
facts.scope: The extra-time moment that completed Madrid’s comeback.
facts.evidence: The official report says Benzema converted a penalty.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Madrid complete the comeback against City?
facts.scope: The second leg of the 2021/22 Champions League semi-final.
facts.evidence: The match report is dated 4 May 2022.

lessons.title: Benzema scores in a Nations League final
lessons.subtitle: France defeat Spain in 2021

story.title: A final in Milan
story.body: France faced Spain in the UEFA Nations League final on 10 October 2021.

story.title: A quick response
story.body: After Spain scored first, Benzema equalised for France before Kylian Mbappé scored the winner.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did France beat in the 2021 Nations League final?
facts.scope: The final at San Siro on 10 October 2021.
facts.evidence: UEFA reports France’s 2–1 victory over Spain.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score?
facts.scope: The 2021 UEFA Nations League final.
facts.evidence: UEFA records the final score as Spain 1–2 France.

facts.label: Benzema’s goal
facts.prompt: Which France player scored the equaliser in the final?
facts.scope: France’s response to Spain’s opening goal.
facts.evidence: UEFA credits Benzema with the equalising goal.

story.title: A final Madrid campaign
story.body: In 2005/06, Zidane delivered one of his last standout performances for Madrid against Espanyol.

story.title: Two goals in a rout
story.body: Madrid won 4–0 at the Bernabéu, with Zidane scoring twice, including the goal that sealed the result.

facts.label: Season
facts.prompt: In which season did Zidane score twice against Espanyol?
facts.scope: The league match in Zidane’s last season as a Real Madrid player.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid dates the brace to the 2005/06 campaign.

facts.label: Opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Madrid beat 4–0 in Zidane’s brace match?
facts.scope: The match at the Santiago Bernabéu.
facts.evidence: The club identifies Espanyol as the opponent.

facts.label: Zidane’s goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Zidane score in the match?
facts.scope: Zidane’s contribution to Madrid’s 4–0 victory.
facts.evidence: The official report says Zidane scored a brace.

lessons.title: Zidane’s three straight European Cups as coach
lessons.subtitle: A rare run from 2016 to 2018

story.title: A new role
story.body: After his playing career, Zidane returned to lead Real Madrid from the dugout.

story.title: Three in succession
story.body: He guided the club to Champions League titles in 2016, 2017 and 2018, becoming the first coach to win three successive editions.

facts.label: Consecutive title years
facts.prompt: Which three years did Zidane’s Madrid team win consecutive Champions League titles?
facts.scope: Zidane’s first-team coaching run.
facts.evidence: The club notes his side won three successive titles from 2016 through 2018.

facts.label: Third final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Madrid defeat in the 2018 final to complete the run?
facts.scope: The 2018 Champions League final in Kyiv.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid defeated Liverpool 3–1 in the final.

facts.label: Coaching distinction
facts.prompt: What distinction did Zidane achieve with the 2018 victory?
answers: First coach to win three consecutive European Cups
distractors: First coach to win four European Cups
First coach to win the Champions League as player and referee
First coach to win five consecutive league titles

value.display: First coach to win three consecutive European Cups
value.text: First coach to win three consecutive European Cups

facts.scope: The record associated with Madrid’s 2018 title.
facts.evidence: The club says Zidane became the first coach to win the European Cup in three successive seasons.

lessons.title: Bale’s Club World Cup semi-final hat-trick
lessons.subtitle: Madrid beat Kashima Antlers

story.title: A place in the final
story.body: Madrid faced Kashima Antlers in the 2018 Club World Cup semi-final in Abu Dhabi.

story.title: Bale takes control
story.body: Bale scored a hat-trick, sending Madrid through to the final and earning the tournament’s Golden Ball.

facts.label: Semi-final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Bale score a hat-trick against in the 2018 Club World Cup?
facts.scope: Real Madrid’s 2018 Club World Cup semi-final.
facts.evidence: The club identifies Kashima Antlers as the semi-final opponent.

facts.label: Hat-trick total
facts.prompt: How many goals did Bale score in the semi-final?
facts.scope: Bale’s 2018 Club World Cup semi-final performance.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid says Bale scored a hat-trick.

facts.label: Tournament award
facts.prompt: Which award did Bale receive at the 2018 Club World Cup?
facts.scope: The individual award announced after the tournament.
facts.evidence: The club names Bale the Golden Ball winner.

story.title: A long spell in Madrid
story.body: Bale spent nine years with Real Madrid after arriving in 2013.

story.title: A decorated era
story.body: The club credits him with 19 trophies and names him the best player of the 2018 Champions League final.

facts.label: Years at Madrid
facts.prompt: How many years did Bale play for Real Madrid?
facts.scope: His completed Madrid spell, from 2013 to 2022.
facts.evidence: The farewell announcement says Bale played in Madrid colours for nine years.

facts.label: Trophy count
facts.prompt: How many trophies did Bale win with Real Madrid?
facts.scope: His completed Real Madrid career.
facts.evidence: The club lists 19 trophies.

facts.label: Final award
facts.prompt: Which individual distinction did Bale receive for the 2018 Champions League final?
distractors: Man of the Match in the semi-final
facts.scope: The final in Kyiv against Liverpool.
facts.evidence: The official announcement names Bale best player of the final.

story.title: Madrid return to Europe
story.body: After winning La Novena, Real Madrid met Feyenoord in the 2002 European Super Cup.

story.title: A goal from the left-back
story.body: Roberto Carlos scored in a 3–1 win at the Stade Louis II in Monaco.

facts.label: Opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Madrid beat in the 2002 European Super Cup?
facts.scope: The match in Monaco on 30 August 2002.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid identifies Feyenoord as its opponent.

facts.label: Match score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Madrid’s 2002 Super Cup win?
facts.scope: The European Super Cup at the Louis II stadium.
facts.evidence: The club records a 3–1 victory.

facts.label: Goal minute
facts.prompt: In which minute did Roberto Carlos score?
facts.scope: Roberto Carlos’s goal in the final.
facts.evidence: The match report lists his goal at minute 21.

story.title: A famous national team
story.body: Roberto Carlos represented Brazil, winning the 2002 FIFA World Cup.

story.title: A role in the final
story.body: He started the 2–0 final victory over Germany at left-back.

facts.label: World Cup year
facts.prompt: In what year did Roberto Carlos win the World Cup with Brazil?
facts.scope: Brazil’s fifth World Cup title, in which Roberto Carlos was a starter.
facts.evidence: FIFA identifies Brazil as the 2002 champion and lists Roberto Carlos in the final squad.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Brazil defeat in the 2002 World Cup final?
facts.scope: The final in Yokohama on 30 June 2002.
facts.evidence: FIFA records Germany as Brazil’s 2002 World Cup final opponent.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Brazil’s 2002 final victory?
facts.scope: The World Cup final in Yokohama.
facts.evidence: FIFA records Brazil’s 2–0 final victory over Germany.

lessons.title: Di Stéfano opens his Madrid account
lessons.subtitle: A friendly against Nancy in 1953

story.title: A first appearance
story.body: Alfredo Di Stéfano made his Real Madrid debut in a friendly against Nancy on 23 September 1953.

story.title: A goal on day one
story.body: He scored his first goal for Madrid with a header in that same match.

facts.label: Debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Di Stéfano face in his Real Madrid debut?
facts.scope: A friendly at the Santiago Bernabéu on 23 September 1953.
facts.evidence: The club says his debut was against Nancy.

facts.label: Debut date
facts.prompt: On what date did Di Stéfano make his Real Madrid debut?
facts.scope: His first friendly appearance for Madrid.
facts.evidence: Real Madrid dates the friendly to 23 September 1953.

facts.label: First Madrid goal
facts.prompt: How did Di Stéfano score his first Real Madrid goal?
facts.scope: His first goal, scored against Nancy in his debut match.
facts.evidence: The club says his first goal was a header.

lessons.title: Di Stéfano’s European Cup record
lessons.subtitle: Di Stéfano’s player-specific European Cup final scoring record and eleven-season honours

story.title: A record across finals
story.body: Di Stéfano scored at least once in every European Cup final he played for Madrid.

story.title: A decorated spell
story.body: In eleven seasons, he won eighteen trophies with the club.

facts.label: European Cup finals
facts.prompt: What scoring record did Di Stéfano achieve in Madrid’s European Cup finals?
answers: Scored at least once in each final
distractors: Kept a clean sheet in each final
Was named player of the match each time
facts.scope: The finals of the European Cup during Di Stéfano’s Madrid career.
facts.evidence: The club profile states that he scored at least one goal in all the European Cup finals.

facts.label: Madrid seasons
facts.prompt: How many seasons did Di Stéfano play for Real Madrid?
facts.scope: His completed Madrid spell, from 1953 to 1964.
facts.evidence: The profile records eighteen trophies across eleven seasons.

facts.label: Trophies
facts.prompt: How many trophies did Di Stéfano win in his eleven Madrid seasons?
facts.scope: His completed Real Madrid playing spell.
facts.evidence: The profile says he won eighteen trophies in eleven seasons.

lessons.title: Xavi creates the second goal in Rome
lessons.subtitle: Barcelona win the 2009 Champions League

story.title: A European final
story.body: Barcelona faced Manchester United in the Champions League final in Rome on 27 May 2009.

story.title: Xavi supplies the assist
story.body: Xavi set up Lionel Messi’s second goal in a 2–0 win and was named man of the match by UEFA’s technical group.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Barcelona beat in the 2009 Champions League final?
facts.scope: The final at Rome’s Stadio Olimpico on 27 May 2009.
facts.evidence: UEFA records a 2–0 Barcelona win over Manchester United.

facts.label: Assist recipient
facts.prompt: Whose goal did Xavi set up in the final?
facts.scope: Barcelona’s second goal in the 2009 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA says Xavi set up Messi’s goal.

facts.label: UEFA award
facts.prompt: Which match award did Xavi receive after the final?
facts.scope: His individual recognition for the 2009 final.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s Technical Study Group selected Xavi man of the match.
